newsitem.title: USA: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN FLAT-OFF $0.50 - DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: US MIDWEST DIRECT HOGS SEEN FLAT-OFF $0.50 - DEALERS.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by sluggish pork demand and large hog marketings, livestock dealers said.
"We're in pretty good shape for tomorrow (Thursday) and starting to work on getting hogs bought for Friday," a packer buyer said in the interior Iowa/southern Minnesota area.
Interior Iowa/southern Minnesota hog receipts Tuesday totalled 115,000 head, compared with the estimate of 100,000, USDA reported. Wednesday's estimate was 110,000 head.
Top prices for hogs delivered to plants in Iowa/southern Minnesota Thursday were seen steady to $0.50 lower at $57.00 to $57.50, the dealers said.

Illinois top prices for hogs at plants were seen steady after prices there dropped $1.00 Wednesday to $55.50, sources there said. Illinois top hog values at the plant have fallen $1.50 since Monday's close, USDA statisticvs showed.
Indiana/Ohio prices on hogs delivered to plants were expected steady-$0.50 lower, with a top of $56.00 to $56.50.
"We got buried with hogs today, it doesn't look like it will be worth a darn tomorrow," an Indiana hog buyer said.
Pork prices at midday were mostly lower in light trading, market sources said.

Fresh loins at midday were quoted unevenly steady, butts were mostly steady to $2.00 per cwt higher, hams were $1.00 lower, lean trimmings were $2.00 lower and pork bellies were generally steady, USDA said in its central U.S. carlot pork report. There were 48.5 loads of pork cuts and 24.0 loads of trimmed and processed pork sold.
